messages:
Leo G: ran a short-form perf matrix vs prod traffic (50k reqs) focusing on sub-100-token requests. surprising hotspot: tokenization + protobuf parse + tiny-write syscall chain is ~70% of host CPU p50.
Nina K: raw numbers? want to see p50/p90 and syscall counts.
Leo G: p50 total 10.8ms, gpu 3.6ms, host 6.8ms. breaking host: Tokenize=3.0ms, ParseProto=1.3ms, HTTP2/gRPC framing=0.7ms, writev/syscalls=1.2ms, misc scheduling=0.6ms. p90 host ~12.5ms. syscalls per request avg=5, bursts when many small frames stream in.
Devon: Note: our canonical kernel chooser always picks MEDIUM for 1-512 seqs. that's likely suboptimal for <=64. we should add a fast-small kernel path.
Leo G: agreed. quick patch idea: use histogram of observed seq_len in the request window and prefer KERNEL_SMALL when majority <=64. also expose override via runtime flag.
Javier: how about tokenization caching? we could cache tokenized prefixes per-tenant up to N entries. would cut tokenize time for short prompt templates.
Nina K: caching is good but watch memory and invalidation on vocab changes. need model-version pinning. also TTL/jitter to avoid eviction stampedes.
Devon: for stream chunking: grpc currently flushes each chunk immediately. we can add a tiny coalescer that waits up to 1.5ms or until size>4k. measured tradeoff: reduces writev count by ~45% and host CPU by ~0.9ms p50, tail latency increases ~0.6ms for some requests.
Leo G: added adaptive rule: if client-specified SLO < 20ms -> flush immediately; else use coalesce. pseudocode: `if client_slo_ms <= 20 => flush_immediate else accumulate(max_ms=1.5, max_bytes=4096)`
Javier: KV cache notes: hot-shard contention when many short requests share prefix hash. solution: per-shard admission limit + leaky admission token so hot key doesn't cause thrash. also add per-key LRU with probabilistic TTL jitter.
Nina K: I ran flamegraphs. majority of host cycles are in Tokenizer::encode loop and in proto::parse allocations. quick wins: (1) fast-path for already-tokenized payloads (flag in header), (2) allocate parser buffers from arena reuse, (3) grpc coalesce + writev batching.
Devon: sample parser fast-path patch (very small):
```
// req_handler.cpp
if (headers.contains("x-tokenized") && headers["x-tokenized"]=="1") {
  req.tokenized = true; // skip Tokenize()
} else {
  Tokenize(req.raw);
}
```
Nina K: ops-bot please create canary plan with these three changes: small-kernel-select, tokenized-fastpath, grpc-coalesce-adaptive.
ops-bot: Canary job created -> canary-9, duration=2h, targets=canary-pool-3, changes=[small-kernel-select,v1; tokenized-fastpath,v1; grpc-coalesce,v1]. monitor=latency, cpu, syscalls, kvcache-miss.
Leo G: I'll own kernel selector config + telemetry.
Devon: i'll own parser fast-path + unit tests.
Javier: i'll own kvcache admission changes + flamegraph dashboard.
Nina K: next steps: land PRs behind feature flags, run canary, collect perf runs (flamegraphs, syscall traces, kv metrics), then iterate. file PRs and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
